bullets: Memory stores instructions, data and intermediate results.
Registers inside the CPU provide very fast working storage.
Cache holds frequently used data and instructions to reduce main-memory access time. RAM is volatile working memory; ROM is nonvolatile memory commonly used for firmware.
Secondary storage such as SSDs keeps files when power is removed.

Buses carry data, addresses and control signals between components.

operators.title: Operators in C

sections.title: Definition
bullets: An operator specifies an operation on one or more operands.
For example, in a + b, + is the operator and a and b are operands.

rows: Integer division truncates toward zero; remainder requires integer operands.
Combine or negate conditions; zero means false. && and || short-circuit.
Store or update a value. = assigns; == compares.
Prefix yields the updated value; postfix yields the old value.
Operate on integer bits; these differ from logical operators.
Size in bytes, address, dereference and member/element access.

sections.title: Precedence and safe use
bullets: Multiplication, division and remainder bind more tightly than addition/subtraction.
Relational comparisons precede equality; logical AND precedes logical OR.
Use parentheses to make intent clear.
Avoid division by zero and expressions that modify one variable multiple times without sequencing.

union.title: Structures versus unions

sections.title: Explanation in simple steps
bullets: A structure gives each member separate storage, so all members can hold values simultaneously. Union members overlap storage; generally use the member most recently written. Structures suit student records; unions suit alternative representations with a separate tag.

bullets: A compiler translates source code into another representation, commonly object/machine code, before the resulting program runs. A traditional interpreter executes source or an intermediate representation under an interpreter at runtime.
Compiled execution commonly has less translation overhead; an interpreter commonly enables quick interactive execution.
Compilation reports translation errors; runtime errors can occur in either approach. C commonly uses compilation and linking; Python commonly uses bytecode plus an interpreter.
Languages are not inherently restricted to one implementation technique.

storage.title: Storage classes

sections.title: Explanation in simple steps
bullets: The traditional introductory classes are auto, register, static and extern.

Automatic block objects (auto or ordinary locals) have block scope and lifetime until block exit; without initialization their values are not given a known initial value. register has the same duration/scope, requests fast access, and its address cannot be taken in C11. A static local has block scope but whole-program lifetime and defaults to zero; it keeps state between calls. A file-scope static object has internal linkage. extern declares an object defined elsewhere and normally has external linkage; its actual static-duration definition defaults to zero if not explicitly initialized.
Scope depends on declaration position, not only the keyword.

recursion.title: Recursion versus iteration

sections.title: Explanation in simple steps
bullets: Recursion calls the same function directly or indirectly and needs a reachable base case.
Iteration repeats via loops and needs a terminating condition.
Factorial is O(n) time in both forms; the straightforward recursive version uses O(n) call-stack space, iterative factorial O(1).
Recursion can clearly express trees and divide-and-conquer algorithms; disadvantages include call overhead and stack exhaustion.
Iteration is often simpler for linear repetition.
Tail-call elimination is not guaranteed by C.
